en.title: ou
en.summary: This is the letter L322 from the vowel-consonant groups.

sections.title: The sound of ou
paragraphs: The letters ou usually sound like the sound /aʊ/. You hear this main sound in the word (out) /aʊt/, which means outside. This letter pair has four different sounds in English words. Most words use the first sound.

sections.title: How to say ou
paragraphs: To say the first sound, open your mouth wide. Then move your lips into a small round circle. For the second sound, push your lips far forward into a tight circle. For the third sound, keep your mouth slightly open and relaxed. For the fourth sound, make a very quick weak sound with relaxed lips. Touch your neck to feel your voice buzz.

sections.title: Spelling rules for ou
paragraphs: In most stressed syllables, ou makes the sound /aʊ/, as in (loud) /laʊd/. In borrowings and several common words, ou sounds like /uː/, as in (group) /ɡruːp/. Before consonants in some native words, ou makes the sound /ʌ/, that is a short stressed sound, as in (touch) /tʌtʃ/ or (cousin) /kʌz.ən/. In unstressed endings, ou sounds like the weak sound /ə/, that is a quick relaxed sound, as in (famous) /feɪ.məs/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with ou
paragraphs: Do not turn the main vowel sound into a single flat vowel. Start wide and glide smoothly to a round lip shape. Do not make the weak ending sound too strong. Keep that unstressed ending very short and quiet.
